subject: Interview with School Committee Candidate Melanie Perkins-McLaughlin
overview: School Committee incumbent Melanie Perkins-McLaughlin discussed her background in child advocacy and her priorities for a second term, emphasizing systemic equity and student mental health.

items.title: Candidate Background and Introduction
items.summary: Danielle Balocca introduces Melanie Perkins-McLaughlin, detailing her professional work as a documentary filmmaker and her personal history as a ward of the state and foster child.

items.title: Path to Local Government
items.summary: McLaughlin explains how her experience advocating for her daughter's special education needs and witnessing systemic inequities led her to join the School Committee.

items.title: First Term Review and Future Priorities
items.summary: The candidate reviews pandemic-era achievements, including the Universal Safety Committee, and identifies mental health support and high school infrastructure as primary future concerns.

items.title: Workforce Diversification and Equity
items.summary: McLaughlin discusses using the School Committee's policy-making and budget powers to diversify the teaching workforce and promote allyship with the BIPOC community.

items.title: Elimination of Credit Recovery Fees
items.summary: McLaughlin advocates for eliminating the $250 fee charged to students for summer credit remediation, arguing that data shows it creates a barrier for the most vulnerable families.

items.title: Family and Community Engagement Audit
items.summary: The candidate mentions an upcoming audit conducted with the Department of Elementary and Secondary Education to improve district communication with underrepresented families.

items.title: Personal Reflections and Advocacy
items.summary: McLaughlin shares personal anecdotes about overcoming a fear of bridges and reaffirms her commitment to serving as a lifelong advocate for marginalized students.
